title: Lightning Rod Guide — Rod Limits, Charge-up, Lightning Arrow and Boss Setup
summary: Lightning Rod is a deployed-object skill: you place a lightning pillar at a location, it charges up, and Lightning Arrow (or any chain that reaches it) triggers a burst from the rod. This guide explains the rod limit, the charge-up requirement, why pre-0.4 'instant trigger all rods' videos are outdated, how Lightning Arrow actually triggers the burst, the Mirage Archer interaction limits, and the mapping vs bossing rod counts.
description: Lightning Rod deep guide: deployed-object rules and rod limit, charge-up and burst trigger, Lightning Arrow chain interaction, 0.4 changes that invalidated old instant-trigger videos, support choices (Scattershot / Chain / Concentrated Area), Weapon Set ownership, combo sequence, mapping vs bossing counts, Mirage Archer known limits, troubleshooting and community evidence.

sections.title: Quick Answer: Place Rods, Then Trigger With Lightning Arrow
paragraphs: Lightning Rod is not a direct-damage attack — it is a deployed object. You place a rod at a location; it charges up; when Lightning Arrow (or a chain that reaches it) passes through, the rod releases a burst.
So the loop is: pre-place a few rods, then fire Lightning Arrow through the rods and the enemies. If the rod has not finished charging, or Lightning Arrow never chains to it, you get no burst.

sections.title: Rod Object Rules
paragraphs: Each use drops one lightning rod at the targeted ground location. The rod exists for a limited duration and can only burst after it finishes charging up.

There is a hard limit on how many rods can exist at once. Old videos showing a screen full of instantly-firing rods were made before the 0.4 cap and charge-up changes and no longer reflect the current client.

sections.title: Player, Mirage and Cap Relationship
paragraphs: The rod cap counts rods from all sources, including ones created by a Mirage Archer clone. If your Mirage is also dropping rods, you can hit the shared cap faster and starve your own placement.
Because the cap is shared, plan rod counts around it: in boss fights you usually want your own rods first, then let the Mirage add a few if headroom remains.

keyValues.label: Bossing count
notes: Place rods on the boss path, not scattered.

sections.title: Lightning Arrow Trigger Logic
paragraphs: Lightning Arrow fires an arrow that chains lightning to nearby enemies. When that chain reaches a charged rod, the rod bursts. The burst is the rod's own lightning damage, separate from the arrow and the chain.

The trigger requires the rod to be charged and the chain to actually reach it. Dense packs help because the chain jumps between enemies and is more likely to touch a rod; a lone rod far from the fight may never be chained.
Mirage-created Lightning Arrow interacting with player rods (and vice versa) has known limits on the current client — treat cross-owner rod triggering as unreliable and verify per patch.

sections.title: Mechanics: Charge-up, Burst and Frequency
paragraphs: A rod's value comes entirely from its burst, so burst frequency equals how often Lightning Arrow reaches a charged rod. More rods in the chain path means more frequent bursts, up to the cap.
Because 0.4 forced rods to charge up, the old 'place rod, instant burst' playstyle is gone. You now pre-place rods slightly ahead of the fight so they are charged by the time Lightning Arrow arrives.
Burst damage and radius scale with the skill's level and supports; the rod itself does not move, so placement is the main skill expression.

sections.title: Weapon Set and Skill Ownership
paragraphs: Rods belong to the weapon set that carries Lightning Rod. A rod's damage and supports come from that set, not from wherever Lightning Arrow is slotted.

Keep Lightning Rod and Lightning Arrow on the same bow set so the rod's supports and the triggering arrow stay consistent. Splitting them across sets is a common source of 'my rods do no damage' reports.

sections.title: Mapping Rotation
paragraphs: In fast mapping you often skip rods entirely and just clear with Lightning Arrow, because placing and charging rods slows the screen clear. Rods pay off when a pack is dense or a rare is tanky.
When you do use them mapping, pre-place 2-3 rods at a chokepoint, then chain through. Do not stop to place a full cap of rods while mapping.

sections.title: Where It Is Used
paragraphs: Lightning Rod is the single-target and stationary-DPS backbone of Lightning Arrow Deadeye and many Ice Shot leveling builds. It turns Lightning Arrow from a clear skill into a burst tool on rares and bosses.
It is also slotted in some Lightning Arrow farmer setups where sustained rod bursts replace repetitive arrow spam on tanky targets.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: The biggest community mismatch is old footage: pre-0.4 videos show rods firing instantly and in large numbers. On the current client the cap and charge-up make that impossible, so players following those videos see 'rods that do nothing'.

The second cluster is Mirage Archer: players expect a Mirage's Lightning Arrow to trigger their rods (or vice versa) and hit current interaction limits. Treat cross-owner triggering as unreliable until a patch note confirms it.
